request.focus: Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) enable language-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data

passages.text: Preprint T WICE U PON A T IME : C OMPLEMENTARY R EPRESEN - TATIONS FOR T IME -S ERIES R EASONING Hedi Zisling ∗ Ben-Gurion University Liran Nochumsohn ∗ Ben-Gurion University Ilan Naiman Google Mihir Parmar Google Omri Azencot Ben-Gurion University A BSTRACT Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) enable language-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data, yet a fundamental question remains: what in- formation should their time-series representations preserve, and what variation should they factor out? Existing TSLMs typically expose the language model to a single representation, imposing a fixed inductive bias across downstream tasks. We instead introduce complementary representations as a design

Bold marks the best result in each panel, excluding GPT-5 (T+V), shown in gray, which is a large proprietary model included as a reference rather than a size-matched comparison. representation—not only model scale or training strategy—is a key determinant of time-series rea- soning ability. This motivates a more fundamental question: Can complementary representations improve general-purpose time-series reasoning? We hypothesize that general-purpose time-series reasoning benefits from exposing the model to com- plementary views of the same signal, each preserving different information and inducing different invariances. Rather than requiring a single representation to simultaneously retain all information relevant to downstream reasoning while suppressing nuisance variation, this formulation allows dis- tinct views to provide different inductive biases. passages.text: Preprint • Complementary representations for time-series reasoning. We establish complemen- tary representation as a design principle for TSLMs, motivated by the observation that quantitative readout requires the original measurement frame, whereas reasoning about temporal dynamics benefits from factoring it out. • A dual-view time-series language model. We propose a dual-tower architecture that combines line plots and normalized delay embeddings within a shared language model. Dedicated visual encoders, compact visual tokens, and multi-level feature fusion integrate temporal structure with the original measurement frame. • State-of-the-art TSLM performance.
